questions.question: In Python, an if-statement always requires a colon (:) at the end of the condition line.
Python's if-statement supports the use of the logical operator 'and' to combine multiple conditions.
The if-statement in Python requires curly braces {} to define the scope of its block.
In Python, if the if condition evaluates to False, the code inside the else block (if provided) will be executed.
Python allows nested if-statements inside the body of another if-statement.
The 'elif' clause is mandatory in Python if-statements when an else clause is used.
In Python, the condition in an if-statement can be any expression that evaluates to a Boolean value.
In Python, the code 'if 5 > 3:' will not execute its code block because the condition must always compare a variable.
An if-statement in Python can combine multiple conditions using logical operators without requiring parentheses for the expression to work properly.
Consider the code snippet: 'if x = 10: print(x)'. This snippet is valid Python syntax.
